title: Live 12.4.6 did not move the object model, as far as two recordings taken against different sets can show
set: the open demo song, not the specimen set the upgrade runbook asks for
question: Did the 12.4.5 to 12.4.6 upgrade add or remove anything in Live's object model that the catalog would have to follow?

result.verdict: negative, and weaker than a runbook re-verification
result.means: Nothing was added and nothing removed by 12.4.6 that these two recordings can see. This is not a substitute for step 2 of the upgrade runbook, and it does not license skipping one.

readings.weight: none on its own. The run was taken against the open demo song rather than the specimen set, so every proposal is a set artefact. The deletion proposals are visibly so: they read 'song.tracks[11].clip_slots[0].clip.<member> is None here', which is an empty clip slot and not a missing property.

readings.reading: class-by-class diff of the two describe recordings, computed offline 2026-09-17
readings.method: Every object each recording describes was grouped by its Live class, and the union of its properties, children and methods was compared per class.

observed.direction: the August recording had more members; today's had none the August one lacked
members_only_in_august: and the add/remove/has listener triplet of each of those nine

readings.interpretation: View is polymorphic per device. The nine properties come from a Simpler and an Eq8 that the specimen set held and the demo song does not, so that is a set difference and not a Live change. The classes reached by only one recording are the same story: each of the eight only in the August recording is a device class, a drum pad or chain inside one, or the Groove in the pool, all of which that set held; WarpMarker is reached only in today's recording, at song.tracks[10].arrangement_clips[0].warp_markers[0]; the specimen set also carried a warped clip, so why the August run reached no marker is not established here and is a recorder or path question rather than a Live change.

verification_notes: The class-by-class diff was recomputed independently on 2026-09-17 and the verdict reproduces: of the 17 classes both recordings reach, exactly one differs, and only in the direction of the 2026-08-30 recording having more members. Nothing appears under 12.4.6 that the earlier recording lacks, which is the direction a Live addition would show in.
An earlier draft of this record said 18 shared classes. That counted NoneType, which the recorder files for a member that resolved to nothing on the specimen; the real figure is 17.

It reproduces only when a member is counted regardless of which bucket the recorder put it in: the recorder files a member under 'children' when it resolves on the specimen and under 'properties' when it does not, so the three lists have to be unioned per class before they are compared.

reproducibility.detail: No saved set on this machine carries a matching name; the seven non-factory sets are music projects. measurements/catalog-live-12.4.5.json records live_version, script_version and rows, and no field naming the set the run was taken against, although step 2 of docs/upgrading_live.md asks for exactly that.
reproducibility.consequence: The 2026-08-30 run is not reproducible. The next upgrade cannot re-measure against what this one measured against, and has to build a specimen set from the runbook's table first.
reproducibility.recordings_are_not_in_the_repository: sync-run3.json and sync-12.4.6.json both sit outside version control, so the diff above cannot be re-run from a clone either.

recorded_also_in: docs/limits.md, section 5, 'Did Live 12.4.6 move the object model?'
still_owed: docs/upgrading_live.md has to carry the finding that no saved specimen set exists and that a report records no set identity. That file is owned elsewhere and the sentences for it were handed over rather than written here.

class_inventory.why: Both raw recordings are unavailable to a later reader: sync-run*.json is gitignored and the 12.4.6 recording lived only in a session scratchpad. This inventory is what the comparison actually rests on, so the verdict can be checked without them.
